raw_response:
I’m still going to farm the steady way this year. Most of my land stays in wheat-maize, because that is what I know best and it keeps grain coming in. I only keep 2 mu in garlic near the house. Garlic can make some money, but it needs more hand work, and at my age with only 2 people at home, I cannot spread too much land into it. I have a well, so I can water when the crop really needs it, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water carelessly.

For wheat, I do roughly what has worked on my fields before: not too little fertilizer, because if wheat turns yellow later it is hard to recover, but not so much that I waste cash. I put base fertilizer before sowing, then one more topdressing around jointing if the stand looks worth pushing. After wheat harvest, maize must go in fast. That turnaround is tight here, so I won’t do heavy tillage. I’ll get the field turned quickly or directly seeded and keep maize simple. For garlic, I only do a small patch because it needs more looking after, more hand labor, and more water. I will spend money on it, but only on a small area so I still keep cash in hand.
